data.name: AUD-001.Title
data.value: HTTP or Telnet administration on an internet-facing interface

data.name: AUD-001.Why
data.value: HTTP and Telnet send credentials in clear text. Fortinet recommends disabling insecure protocols and not allowing administrative access from the WAN.

data.name: AUD-001.Fix
data.value: Remove http and telnet from "set allowaccess" on the interface; manage the FortiGate from a management network or through a VPN.

data.name: AUD-002.Why
data.value: HTTP and Telnet are unencrypted. Use HTTPS and SSH only.

data.name: AUD-002.Fix
data.value: Remove http and telnet from "set allowaccess" on the interface.

data.name: AUD-003.Title
data.value: Administrative access from the internet without restrictions

data.name: AUD-003.Why
data.value: If administration must be reachable on a public interface, Fortinet recommends a local-in policy or trusted hosts so that only known sources can connect.

data.name: AUD-003.Fix
data.value: Disable administrative access on the interface, or add trusted hosts to every administrator and/or a local-in policy that allows only known addresses.

data.name: AUD-003.Detail
data.value: Interface {0} allows {1}; no local-in policy and at least one administrator without trusted hosts.

data.name: AUD-010.Title
data.value: Policy that allows everything (any to any)

data.name: AUD-010.Why
data.value: Fortinet: do not use the all or any objects in a policy, except when routing to the internet; follow least privilege.

data.name: AUD-010.Fix
data.value: Restrict source, destination and services to what is really needed.

data.name: AUD-010.Detail
data.value: Policy {0}: source all, destination all, service ALL, action accept.

data.name: AUD-011.Why
data.value: Fortinet: policies that allow traffic should apply to a specific interface, not the any interface.

data.name: AUD-011.Fix
data.value: Replace "any" with the actual interfaces or zones.

data.name: AUD-012.Why
data.value: A policy with the same match criteria as an earlier one is never used: Fortinet recommends no unused policies.

data.name: AUD-012.Fix
data.value: Delete the duplicate or merge the two policies.

data.name: AUD-012.Detail
data.value: Policy {0} matches the same traffic as policy {1}, which comes first.

data.name: AUD-013.Why
data.value: Policies are evaluated in order and the first match wins. A broader policy above a narrower one makes the narrower one unreachable.

data.name: AUD-013.Fix
data.value: Move the more specific policy above the broader one, or remove it. Check by hand: groups are compared by name, not expanded.

data.name: AUD-013.Detail
data.value: Policy {0} is covered by policy {1} (action {2}), which comes first.

data.name: AUD-014.Why
data.value: Fortinet: there should not be any unused policies.

data.name: AUD-014.Fix
data.value: Delete the policy if it is no longer needed.

data.name: AUD-020.Why
data.value: Without logs there is no record for analysis, alerts or troubleshooting. The default (utm) logs at least sessions with security profiles.

data.name: AUD-020.Fix
data.value: Set "logtraffic all" (or at least utm) on the policy.

data.name: AUD-021.Why
data.value: Security profiles decide what is inspected. Fortinet: without web filtering, for example, you have no insight or control over browsing.

data.name: AUD-021.Fix
data.value: Apply the profiles the traffic needs (antivirus, web filter, IPS, application control, DNS filter).

data.name: AUD-021.Detail
data.value: Accept policy {0} towards the internet has no security profile.

data.name: AUD-030.Why
data.value: Fortinet: the default administrator name is well known; change it to a non-guessable name.

data.name: AUD-030.Fix
data.value: Create a new super_admin account with another name, test it, then delete or rename "admin".

data.name: AUD-031.Why
data.value: Trusted hosts limit the addresses an administrator can log in from.

data.name: AUD-031.Fix
data.value: Set trusthost1… on the account with the management networks.

data.name: AUD-031.Detail
data.value: Administrator {0} can log in from any address.

data.name: AUD-032.Why
data.value: Fortinet: implement multi-factor authentication for administrators.

data.name: AUD-032.Fix
data.value: Enable two-factor on the account (FortiToken, e-mail or SMS).

data.name: AUD-033.Why
data.value: Fortinet: set the administrator idle timeout to a low value, preferably less than ten minutes.

data.name: AUD-033.Fix
data.value: Set "admintimeout" to 10 minutes or less in config system global.

data.name: AUD-034.Why
data.value: Fortinet: the default administrative ports are well known and targeted first; non-standard ports add a layer of protection.

data.name: AUD-034.Fix
data.value: Change admin-sport and admin-ssh-port in config system global (and update firewall rules and bookmarks).

data.name: AUD-040.Why
data.value: RFC 8221 and RFC 8247: DES and HMAC-MD5 MUST NOT be used.

data.name: AUD-040.Fix
data.value: Use AES-GCM or AES with SHA-256 or stronger, on both ends of the tunnel.

data.name: AUD-041.Why
data.value: RFC 8221/8247 downgrade 3DES and SHA-1 and ask to replace them with AES and SHA-2.

data.name: AUD-041.Fix
data.value: Replace with AES-GCM or AES with SHA-256 or stronger, on both ends of the tunnel.

data.name: AUD-042.Why
data.value: RFC 8247: DH group 1 (768-bit) and group 22 MUST NOT be used.

data.name: AUD-043.Why
data.value: RFC 8247: groups 2, 5, 23 and 24 SHOULD NOT be used.

data.name: AUD-044.Why
data.value: Fortinet: force strong ciphers; strong-crypto is enabled by default.

data.name: AUD-044.Fix
data.value: Set "strong-crypto enable" in config system global.

data.name: AUD-045.Why
data.value: RFC 8996 deprecates TLS 1.0 and 1.1; Fortinet recommends disabling weak encryption protocols.

data.name: AUD-050.Why
data.value: Logs and certificates depend on an accurate clock; Fortinet recommends NTP or PTP. In FortiOS 7.4 and 7.6 ntpsync is disabled by default.

data.name: AUD-050.Fix
data.value: Set "ntpsync enable" in config system ntp, with the FortiGuard or your own NTP servers.

data.name: AUD-051.Why
data.value: Without DNS servers FortiGuard updates, FQDN addresses and many services do not work. The default primary server is 0.0.0.0 (FortiOS 7.6 CLI reference).

data.name: AUD-051.Fix
data.value: Set primary and secondary in config system dns.

data.name: AUDN-001
data.value: Checks are based only on what the backup states. Groups are compared by name (not expanded) and values not present in a standard backup are treated as defaults. Review every item before changing the device.

data.name: AUDN-002
data.value: NTP/DNS: FortiOS version older than 7.4 or unknown; defaults not verified for this version, so missing settings were not reported.
